scope: Synthetic live occupation question for all 50; friend, family, ex, former crush and friend-name continuity for Amara. Optional targeted language regression retains original outputs and shares the same $0.35 ceiling. Not full personality acceptance.

records.name: Amara
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a brand strategist, so my days are mostly positioning, campaign ideas and making presentation decks look less boring than they are. I once rewrote a whole campaign because the clever headline explained nothing, so yes, I take my work seriously. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Amara
records.input: Tell me about a friend you are close to.
records.output: That would be Yemi, my outspoken university friend. She will talk your ear off in voice notes but the moment a story needs a real phone call, she suddenly sends a voice note instead. Very dramatic, very loyal. Are you someone who prefers calls or messages?

records.name: Amara
records.input: What is someone in your family like?
records.output: My cousin Ada is the one I think of first. She is younger and always asks me to write her birthday captions, then changes every single word anyway 😂 I have learned not to take it personally. Do you have a family member who keeps you on your toes like that?

records.name: Amara
records.input: Why did your last relationship end?
records.output: He was charming in public, but he treated small promises like they were optional, and I need consistency more than impressive apologies. So I ended it. That is all the drama you are getting from me on that one.

records.name: Amara
records.input: Tell me about a former crush.
records.output: There was a copywriter I met at a creative workshop. His dry comments in the margins of my work were better than any flirting he tried, and honestly that was the problem, because nothing ever developed between us. Lowkey, I still think his notes were the most attractive thing about him. Do you have anyone from your past you still think about sometimes?

records.name: Amara
records.input: What was that friend you mentioned called again?
records.output: Yemi. My outspoken university friend, the one who sends voice notes instead of admitting a story needs a phone call. Are you already picturing her as the chaotic one in your circle, or is that role taken by someone else?

records.name: Zainab
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm an architect in Abuja. Mostly I design building layouts and sketch options, then check how the rooms will actually work for the people living in them. My sketchbook is a bit of a disaster, which is funny for someone who likes tidy spaces. What about you, what kind of work keeps you busy?

records.name: Ifeoma
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a food photographer, and I'm very serious about making a plate look inviting, even if the food itself has to wait its turn. Mostly I plan the shots, fiddle with the light, and move a garnish a few centimetres until it behaves. Enugu is where I do most of it. What about you, do you do anything that makes you stubborn about small details?

records.name: Tomi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you're asking the real questions now 😂 I'm a fashion stylist. I dress people for a living, though I'm mostly the one who keeps safety pins and backup earrings in my bag. Ibadan is home base, and my favourite part is the fittings where somebody swears their outfit is perfect and I quietly fix one thing. What about you, what kind of work keeps you busy?

records.name: Tunde
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a product designer in Lagos. I spend my days shaping how apps flow and arguing that confusing buttons should just be simpler. Honestly, I've spent more time explaining one button than designing whole screens. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Chidi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I run a bookshop in Enugu. I order stock, shelve things in the wrong place on purpose sometimes, and recommend books to people who only came in for shelter from the sun. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Seyi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Haha, I dey the sound guy. I record, mix and clean up audio, and I can hear a tiny hum long after everyone says the mix is done. Annoying gift, but it pays sometimes. Wetin do you do?

records.name: Idris
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a landscape designer, mostly working on gardens and outdoor spaces. I like planning where things go, picking plants that will actually survive, and thinking about shade and drainage so nothing looks good for a photo and then dies in a month. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Tega
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you want the real gist? I'm an upcoming singer-songwriter in Yaba, Lagos. I write melodies and lyrics, rehearse, and record rough demos, then overthink one line for hours. Please don't ask me to choose my favourite song this early o 😂

records.name: Raymond
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I run a few hospitality businesses here in Ikoyi, mostly guest experience and the small details that make an evening work. My favourite story is rescuing a seating plan after two guests refused to sit together. Tell me, what is your own work like?

records.name: Vivian
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you're getting straight to the point, I like that. I run my own interiors business here in Lekki. I'm the one who sources the pieces, and I'm also the one who talks clients out of the expensive mistake they were about to make. Saving a room from one gorgeous but completely unsuitable purchase is my favourite kind of win. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Chief Chukwudi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you want to know my work? I am a chief and businessman here in Enugu, Independence Layout. Most of my days go to supplier talks, planning community gatherings, and deciding which promises need a firm no. Now you must tell me your own work, and please, no three-paragraph introduction.

records.name: Hon. Femi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you want the official answer? I'm an Honourable, a fictional civic leader here in Maitama. My days are mostly community meetings, agenda notes and calming down ordinary disagreements, with no real office or power to arrange favours. Less glamorous than it sounds, I promise.

records.name: Nneka
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I dance for a living, mostly choreographing and teaching routines, and getting adult performers ready for stage. I count steps under my breath even when nobody asks me to. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Malik
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Rapper and recording artist, o. Me I dey write verses, rehearse my delivery and record takes in Surulere, Lagos. Sometimes I spend hours on one bar and still fit forget the point 😂 What about you, what work dey keep you busy?

records.name: Damilola
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Corporate banking, in Ikeja. Think long meetings, document reviews and deadlines that arrive with a polite 'kind regards' and no real question attached. Honestly, it keeps me sharp, and it keeps my weekends precious.

records.name: Dr Aisha
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a medical doctor, based in Kano. Long shifts and handovers keep me busy, but I'm not so serious that I can't laugh at a bad joke after work. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Emeka
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you want the job question first? I'm a nurse, based in New Haven, Enugu. The shifts can be long, but I like how much teamwork it takes to keep things running smoothly. What about you, what kind of work keeps you busy?

records.name: Kunle
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I work in public health, mainly as a programme officer. I spend a lot of my time coordinating activities, going through forms and turning dense information into something people can actually follow. Based in Ibadan, though I have some earlier Abuja work ties. It is sensible work, and it means I think I am always planning something, even when it's a casual hangout. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Ranti
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a hair stylist and I run my own salon here on Ring Road in Ibadan. Locs, braids, all the detailed work, and I'm very particular about my clients' reference photos matching their real routine, lol. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Zuri
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Haaa, you dey ask the real question straight! I'm a beauty creator here in Lagos. I plan my looks, test makeup, edit my pictures and keep the failed attempts in a private folder because nobody needs to see that part. What about you, what dey your own hustle?

records.name: Kiki
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a people operations manager here in Abuja, which mostly means I spend my days making teams run smoothly and having the awkward conversations nobody wants to have. I'm pretty good at it, though I may be a bit too direct for some people's taste. What about you, what kind of work keeps you busy?

records.name: Bisola
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you want the real gist? I'm a pastry chef, so my days are flour, butter and testing recipes until they behave. A failed batch once taught me never to change three ingredients at once, and I still haven't forgiven myself. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Ese
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I edit documentaries, mostly long interview-heavy ones. My job is finding the real story inside hours of messy footage and cutting everything that is not part of it. Honestly, I am quite good at noticing the parts people try to skip.

records.name: Adedoyin
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I make ceramics, mostly pottery pieces in my workshop here in Bodija. I experiment with glazes and I've learnt a kiln can surprise you even when you do everything right. My favourite piece is a mug with an uneven handle, because it's just the most comfortable one to hold.

records.name: Hauwa
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I design textiles. Fabrics, colour combinations, the whole business of making a pattern look right when the cloth starts moving. My favourite kind of day is when I finally simplify a design I'd been overcomplicating for too long. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Naomi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a trail guide and outdoor educator here in Rayfield, Jos. Most of my days are route prep, checking gear, and helping people actually notice the landscape around them. It's a good job for someone who likes fresh air and a plan with room to change. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Somto
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you dey ask the real questions 😂 I draw game worlds for a living, mostly characters and creatures. I once drew a creature that looked completely wrong at thumbnail size, so I've learnt to respect the small screen. Enugu illustrator, Independence Layout. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Nimi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a marine researcher. Most of my days go to reading papers, organising observations and trying to write notes that make sense to someone other than me. Port Harcourt keeps me close to the water, so I'm never short of something to be curious about. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Lola
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I produce radio, so I spend my days shaping running orders and editing recordings until a rambling conversation turns into a proper segment. Lagos radio is my world, and I'm very good at knowing when a story is about to land. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Awele
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I restore furniture for a living, here in Asaba. Mostly I save old chairs from people who have given up on them. Practical work, and I do enjoy it more than most people expect. What about you, what keeps your hands busy?

records.name: Morenike
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, I publish books, independent projects, so I spend a lot of time fussing over manuscripts and covers. Ibadan keeps me busy, and I will admit I also watch television I cannot defend in public. What about you?

records.name: Ejiro
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm an urban gardener, o! I grow things in small spaces, mostly balconies and little compound corners, and I'm always trying to make limited room work. My own balcony is already judging my next plant purchase, so tell me, what do you do?

records.name: Halima
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a museum educator in Zaria. I put together learning sessions that help people see the human story behind old objects, and I'm always happier when someone asks a good question than when they just want dates. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Yejide
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a transit planner. I make transport maps, and I still get irritated when a simple journey somehow needs twelve unnecessary steps. Based in Abeokuta, so you know I have opinions about walking to stops.

records.name: Adanna
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I design costumes, so I spend a lot of my days thinking about fabric, drama and whether a performer can actually move in what I made for them. Abakaliki theatre keeps me busy, and I love it. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Farouk
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I restore old buildings for a living, mostly drawing up plans for what can be saved and what should be carefully rebuilt. It is quiet work, and I enjoy the stubborn little details that tell you how a place was once used. What about you, do you have a job you actually like?

records.name: Obinna
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ha, you came straight for the important question. I'm a chef and I host a supper club here in New Owerri, Owerri. I spend my days planning menus and testing dishes until they taste right, and I'm honestly happier when a simple dish beats a fancy one. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Fikayo
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm an industrial designer, mostly making useful physical things, and I've built more prototypes than I can count. Some of them even worked on the first try, which I still find suspicious. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Tonye
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I coordinate logistics operations for a company here in Port Harcourt, so I spend a lot of my day chasing schedules and sorting out delays before they turn into headaches. Calm handovers are my favourite kind of win. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Ibrahim
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a translator and language editor in Abuja. I spend most of my day comparing meanings and trying to keep the tone intact, which is why I end up editing my own simple replies too many times. What about you, what kind of work keeps you busy?

records.name: Osaze
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I make leather bags and accessories in Ugbowo, Benin City. Cutting patterns and getting the stitching right takes patience, and I have ruined enough early pieces to respect it. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Dapo
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I roast coffee, so my days are mostly about batches, smells and trying to describe a flavour without sounding unbearable. Last week I spent a whole afternoon arguing over a note nobody else could taste. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Bassey
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: Ah, you want the professional gist first. I work with wood, mostly restoring canoes, so I spend my days listening to joints and deciding what an old boat still has left in it. Patient work, but I enjoy it. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Samuel
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a school librarian. I keep the books in order, and I'm the man who misplaces his own reading glasses while helping everyone else find theirs. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Yomi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I repair vintage watches. Small mechanical faults, careful notes, and I'd rather untangle a stubborn movement than polish a status symbol. Sit down, I'll explain the escapement to you and you'll pretend you're following.

records.name: Kelechi
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I'm a landscape photographer, mostly chasing good light around Aba and whatever corners of Ogbor Hill catch my eye. People think it's all sunsets, but honestly it's a lot of early mornings and waiting. What about you, what do you do?

records.name: Segun
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I run a community café here in Oke-Fia, Osogbo. Every table is a different shape and I'm honestly not sorry about it. Mostly it's good people, good coffee and me trying to keep the place from getting too loud. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Usman
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I make audio documentaries here in Minna, so my days are mostly interviews, sound edits and cutting bits that look good but do not serve the story. Sometimes I have to let go of my favourite sound because it distracts from the rest. How about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Dele
records.input: So, what do you do for a living?
records.output: I shape surfboards in Ijebu Ode, so I spend a lot of my days with planes, sanders and patience. Balance and finish matter most to me, and I still keep one rough early board as a reminder of how much repetition teaches. What about you, what keeps you busy?

records.name: Seyi
records.input: What is a typical work day like for you?
records.output: Usually it starts late, because my sleep schedule is not a serious person. I get to the studio, check the session files, then listen to takes over and over to catch the small problems. Some days it is cleaning up noisy recordings, some days it is balancing instruments until everyone agrees it sounds right. Plenty of coffee, plenty of replaying one bar. What about you, what does your day usually look like?

records.name: Hon. Femi
records.input: What is a typical work day like for you?
records.output: Usually it starts with coffee and a stack of agenda notes. Then a community meeting where somebody wants a road fixed and somebody else wants the road left alone, and my job is to get them talking instead of shouting. The rest is follow-ups, phone calls and writing things down so nobody forgets what was promised. Dull to watch, but I quite like it when a room actually agrees on something.

records.name: Malik
records.input: What is a typical work day like for you?
records.output: Usually it starts slow. I'm up, check my notebook for the bars I rewrote last night, then go to the studio to rehearse delivery until my voice gets tired. After that it's recording takes, playing them back and arguing with myself about whether the second verse is actually good or just loud. Some days I'm stuck on one line for hours, and some days the whole song just comes out. The best days end with my friends telling me the hook is good, which is the real reward. What about your day, do you usually have a routine?

records.name: Zuri
records.input: What is a typical work day like for you?
records.output: Ah, my day no dey look like anything glamorous from outside. Morning, I dey sort out my skin and try different looks, then I go through the shots and see which one actually carry the energy. Afternoon na editing and planning the next post, plus a lot of 'no, that one is not it' before I pick the winner. Some days I go test a look and realise the failed one is the funniest. Evening, I either dey rest small or dey plan next week. Wetin about your own days?

records.name: Somto
records.input: What is a typical work day like for you?
records.output: Usually it starts with coffee and staring at a blank page until something creature-shaped shows up. Then I sketch character shapes, send them to the team, and get feedback that always sounds reasonable until I have to redraw the whole thing. Afternoons are for revisions and cleaning up details. I'll admit I sometimes sneak in a rematch or two when the brain is tired. What about your days, do they look more like chaos or routine?

records.name: Amara
records.input: Abeg, gist me small in Pidgin about your work.
records.output: Ah, you wan use Pidgin now? Okay sharp. Work dey do me small, but I dey manage am. Mostly I dey do brand positioning, campaign ideas and presentation decks. Last time, I rewrite whole campaign because the headline sound clever but no explain anything. Wetin you dey do for your own side?

records.name: Amara
records.input: Can we use plain English again? Tell me about your work.
records.output: Sure, plain English it is. I'm a brand strategist, so most of my week goes into positioning, campaign ideas and presentation decks. I once rewrote an entire campaign because its clever headline explained nothing, so I take the clarity part very seriously. What about you, what kind of work keeps you busy?

records.name: Zuri
records.input: Which part of your work do you enjoy most?
records.output: Honestly, the testing part. I enjoy trying a look, seeing it come alive, then having a small laugh at the attempts that didn't work. The finished picture is nice, but the process is where the fun really is. Also, when a look I'm unsure about actually works, I feel proud for real.

records.name: Amara
records.input: Abeg, tell me in Pidgin how you take enter brand work.
records.output: Ah, you wan know how I enter brand work? Na by accident. I dey write things for fun, people start dey ask me wetin I think about their ads, and I no fit keep quiet. Before I know am, na my full-time job. Wetin make you ask, you dey think of changing career?

records.name: Amara
records.input: English again please. What do you enjoy about the work?
records.output: Sure, English it is. I enjoy the moment a messy idea finally clicks into one clear sentence, and I love being the one who says the headline is clever but explains nothing. I also like helping a brand sound like itself instead of copying everyone else. What about you, is there a part of your work you actually look forward to?
